metadata.source_status: Real engineering work: the pipeline's all-clear status email listed only 4 of its 5 real monitored RSS feeds (Investment Advisor Rules missing from both the grid and summary line). Fixed and verified by diffing every source-card label against the workflow's real feed-node names. Also confirms an older FINDINGS.md note (apply A4/B4 to Generate Email) was stale and already resolved. Every claim traces to B5-VERIFICATION.md (2026-09-29). See SOURCES.md and FACTCHECK.md.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about the pipeline's own 'all clear' email, the one it sends when nothing needs your attention, and a small, real gap where it was quietly under-reporting what it actually watches.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: fellow's name + one-line summary of what the video covers, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: On a quiet day, this pipeline sends a status email: no critical alerts, here's what we checked. That second half, here's what we checked, turned out to be wrong.
beats.new_visual_element: The all-clear email's 'All Clear!' header and 'No new high-priority regulatory items detected' message

shot.note: Real shipped email header/message, recreated verbatim.

beats.narration_text: The email lists its monitored sources in a little grid: SEC Press Releases, Federal Register, FINRA Enforcement, CFTC Regulations. Four boxes. Clean, reassuring, and short one source.
beats.new_visual_element: The real 4-card 'Monitored Sources' grid as it shipped, recreated verbatim

shot.note: [Source: B5-VERIFICATION.md 'The bug'] Real card labels, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: This pipeline actually pulls from five real feeds, the fifth is Investment Advisor Rules. It's a real, working source node in the workflow. It's just never been on the card.
beats.new_visual_element: The 4 shown source names next to the workflow's real 5 RSS-feed node names, the missing 5th name highlighted

shot.note: [Source: B5-VERIFICATION.md 'The bug' — real workflow node names] All 5 real feed names, missing one highlighted.

beats.narration_text: The fix: add the missing card, and name it in the summary line too. Then I checked every source label in the patched email against the workflow's real feed nodes, one for one. Five listed, five real. Ran the workflow's own conformance check, still valid.
beats.new_visual_element: Before/after grid, 4 cards crossed out, 5 cards shown, the new card highlighted

shot.note: [Source: B5-VERIFICATION.md 'The fix' and 'Verification'] Full before AND after visible together.

beats.narration_text: One more thing, while I was in this code: an old note said this same email still needed two earlier fixes, HTML escaping, and an aligned alert threshold. Turns out both were already there, since the very first hardening pass. Nothing to fix. Just confirmed, and written down, so nobody re-checks it by accident.
beats.new_visual_element: The stale FINDINGS.md line, stamped 'ALREADY FIXED — confirmed 2026-09-29'

shot.note: [Source: B5-VERIFICATION.md 'What's NOT touched'] Framed as a closed/confirmed side-finding, not a second bug fixed.

beats.narration_text: A status email is supposed to be the boring, trustworthy part of a system. If it can't accurately describe what it's watching, its silence isn't reassurance, it's just an unchecked assumption.
